definition: imbalanced-learn offers resampling methods such as SMOTE for training on datasets where one class is rare.
details: A scikit-learn-contrib project started by Guillaume Lemaître, Fernando Nogueira and Christos Aridas in 2014.

explainer.lead: How to install imbalanced-learn, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
from collections import Counter
from imblearn.over_sampling import SMOTE
from sklearn.datasets import make_classification

X, y = make_classification(weights=[0.95, 0.05], random_state=0)
X_res, y_res = SMOTE(random_state=0).fit_resample(X, y)
print(Counter(y), "->", Counter(y_res))

explainer.inAi: Fraud, defect and rare-disease detection all have tiny positive classes; resampling helps the model notice them.
explainer.jsNote: imbalanced-learn is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.

tiers.eli5: If almost all examples are one kind, the model ignores the rare kind; this toolkit evens the odds by adding or trimming examples.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers drop it into scikit-learn pipelines to oversample or undersample before fitting a classifier. A pitfall is resampling before splitting the data, which leaks synthetic examples into the test set.
tiers.paperLevel: It is a scikit-learn-contrib project offering resampling techniques, including SMOTE, for class-imbalanced datasets, started by Guillaume Lemaître, Fernando Nogueira and Christos Aridas in 2014. Limits include overfitting to synthetic minority samples and distortion of the original distribution.

explainer.example: On a fraud dataset with 1% positives, SMOTE generates synthetic positive cases so the classifier learns the rare class instead of predicting the majority everywhere.
